subject: Recommended model slate + pilot plan for Skyline Health demo
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@skyline.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 15:03:00 +0000
Subject: Recommended model slate & next steps — Skyline demo follow-up

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the time earlier — really appreciated the clear product goals and the latency constraint for interactive triage (target <= 300ms tail for 512-token responses). Quick recap and my recommended next steps below so we keep momentum: 

Recap: we validated the two main flows (symptom triage and document ingestion QA). You flagged accuracy on medical terminology and cost sensitivity for high call volumes.

Recommended shortlist (attached: skyline_model_shortlist_benchmarks.csv):
- Option A: LlamaX-13B-8bit (recommended pilot) — best cost/throughput balance; median latency ~220ms on our Dedicated p3s for 512 tokens, expected cost ~0.6x current baseline.
- Option B: MedTuned-7B-q4 — stronger on named-entity recall for clinical terms in our evals, but ~1.6x cost vs A and slightly higher latency (~290ms).
- Option C: OpenCura-33B-quant — highest quality on long-context extraction (document QA), but cost and latency are materially higher; use for batch jobs rather than interactive.

Why A first: it hits your interactive SLO with room for batching and prefix caching, and allows us to iterate on hallucination guards quickly. B is the fallback when recall is a hard requirement on specific clinical subdomains. C we recommend only for nightly batch ingestion/ensuring extraction quality.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Pilot scope (2 weeks): instrument 500 triage calls/day to run on Option A + evaluation harness we provide (prompt_set_v1.txt attached).
2) Shared evals: we’ll run the in-house benchmark and send a short report in 5 business days.
3) SLA/commercial touch: Ben will follow up with a draft pilot commercial term sheet and provisional pricing.

Attachments: skyline_model_shortlist_benchmarks.csv (benchmarks), prompt_set_v1.txt (eval prompts), pilot_scope_outline.pdf

If this looks reasonable, can we lock the pilot start for Jan 23? I can schedule an onboarding session and request a quick procurement checklist from you.

Thanks,
—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: prompt_set_v1.txt (text, 18KB)

Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0500

Mina,

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications before we commit to a Jan 23 pilot: 
- For Option A, can you confirm the expected 95th percentile latency for the 512-token triage responses (on our preferred region: us-east)? We need to ensure the worst-case user experience is covered.
- For Option B, are there any additional data-privacy controls you recommend given PHI sensitivity? Is MedTuned-7B available in a private deployment?
- Procurement wants a one-page pilot statement of work and a preliminary cost estimate we can use to secure an internal budget hold.

Also adding procurement (procurement@skyline.health) here for visibility.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Gomez
Head of Product, CareFlow | Skyline Health

Hi Aisha — quick follow-up with the specifics you asked for and a slightly more prescriptive pilot plan.

95th percentile latencies (us-east, Dedicated p3 equivalent, 512-token responses):
- Option A (LlamaX-13B-8bit): 95th ~ 360ms (with the conservative sequence-length distribution you described). We can bring that down to ~300ms by enabling aggressive prefix caching for clinical templates and a 4-request batching window.
- Option B (MedTuned-7B-q4): 95th ~ 420ms; benefits on recall but we need to reserve higher compute for spikes.
- Option C (OpenCura-33B-quant): 95th ~ 780ms (not suitable for interactive triage).

Privacy/deployment notes: MedTuned-7B is available in Redwood Private (VPC) which we recommend for PHI-sensitive workloads; Option A can be run in Dedicated with customer-managed network peering and KMS for keys.

Pilot statement of work (one-pager outline):
- Duration: 2 weeks (Jan 23–Feb 5)
- Scope: 500 triage calls/day routed to Option A; full logging (token-level) for internal evals; sampled human review on 5% of calls for clinical accuracy.
- Success criteria: 1) non-degradation of triage accuracy vs current baseline (<3% drop on named-entity recall for core diagnoses), 2) 95th latency <400ms during normal traffic, 3) acceptable cost delta (TBD — Ben to propose).

Links: Pilot playbook & eval dashboard: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SkylinePilotPack
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DEAL-7890

Next asks: 
- Aisha/procurement: confirm pilot start window Jan 23 and we’ll send the one-pager + T&Cs for legal review.
- Ben: I’ll need a preliminary pricing row (est. monthly cost at pilot scale and at steady-state 5k calls/day) to include in the SOW.

Best,
—Mina
Attachment: pilot_scope_outline.pdf (PDF, 45KB)
